newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no trade-private.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no trade-private.

text.p: Nebraska feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were quiet, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, market sources said.
A few packer bids at $105.00 per cwt on a dressed basis were reported but bid were passed with owners asking $108.00-$110.00.
Sales last week ranged $105.00 to $108.00, with the bulk of cattle trading at $106.00 to $107.00, sources said.
Extreme cold and severe wind chill readings late last week and through the weekend stressed cattle and slowed weight gains, they said.
Temperatures were expected to moderate Tuesday, which would ease the stress, they said.
